cf.title: New data type binary format documentation

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal, and the review notes record that Tom Lane and Robert Haas asked for prose documentation of the binary formats. Two fixable design points remain: the patch removes testlibpq3 without a stated reason (maintenance-fit-2), and the chapter introduction does not say whether layouts are stable across versions (standards-compat-2). Confidence is medium because the chapter hunk is truncated and nobody has replied to the July 2026 patch.

brief.title: Document the binary wire format of built-in data types
brief.problem: Driver authors who use the binary protocol must read each type's send and receive functions to learn its layout, because the docs only say integers are big-endian. This affects libpq users and drivers in every language.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds a new chapter, "Binary Format of Data Types", under Client Interfaces, with general conventions and a prose layout for each built-in type, ordered like the Data Types chapter. It links to the new chapter from datatype.sgml and protocol.sgml. It also removes testlibpq3 and libpq Example Program 3 from the docs.
user_visible_surface: New documentation chapter "Binary Format of Data Types" (binary-format.sgml) in the Client Interfaces part.
New index terms "binary format" and "wire format".
libpq Example Program 3 (testlibpq3.c, testlibpq3.sql) is removed from the docs and from src/test/examples.
author_claims: The chapter covers every built-in data type, written in prose without code examples, as Tom Lane and Robert Haas asked.
The server's send and receive functions stay authoritative if the docs and the source disagree.
Mark Wong says he wrote the patch with help from Claude.
brief.thread_state: Only Mark Wong's 2026-07-30 patch message is visible after the 2023 Returned with Feedback; nobody has replied to it. Earlier, Tom Lane, Robert Haas and Peter Eisentraut agreed on prose docs in a separate chapter, but Peter preferred the Data Types chapter.
unclear: The thread does not say why testlibpq3 is removed, though it demonstrates PQexecParams with out-of-line parameters as well as binary I/O, and nobody asked for its removal.
The patch does not say how the chapter will be kept in sync when a type's send or receive function changes.
The visible hunk is truncated, so a reviewer cannot confirm that all built-in types, including composite, range and multirange, are covered.
The patch does not say whether the docs promise that binary formats are stable across server versions.
search_queries: network byte order binary send functions

objections.title: Removing testlibpq3 drops the only built example of binary parameters
objections.failure_scenario: A libpq user looks for a complete program that passes out-of-line or binary parameters through PQexecParams and finds no Example Program 3. Tutorials that link to the libpq-example-3 anchor now get a broken link. The example lived in src/test/examples, where it can still be compiled; the prose that replaces it cannot.
objections.argument: The removed program's own header says it tests "out-of-line parameters and binary I/O", so it covers more than type layouts. In message #10 the plan was to leave testlibpq3.c as it was, and no reviewer asked for its removal. The commit message gives no reason for the removal. Keeping the example costs little, and removing it is unrelated to documenting formats.
objections.author_must_show: Why must testlibpq3 go in the same patch, and what libpq example then shows binary parameters and out-of-line parameters with PQexecParams?

critic.reasoning: The commit message and file list confirm testlibpq3 is removed, and its header says it also shows out-of-line parameters with PQexecParams. No reviewer asked for removal and the patch gives no reason; keeping the example would fix this.

objections.title: Chapter does not say whether binary layouts are stable across versions
objections.failure_scenario: A driver author builds a binary decoder from the version 20 chapter and assumes it covers every server the driver supports. A later release changes one type's send function, and the driver either breaks or the change is blocked as a documented contract break. Nobody notices until users report wrong values.
objections.argument: protocol.sgml keeps its warning that complex binary representations may change across server versions, but the new chapter presents each layout as fact with no versioning note. Published per-type prose is likely to be read by driver authors as a contract, which is stronger than today's source-code-only status in message #5. The chapter says the source wins on disagreement, but says nothing on change policy or history.
objections.author_must_show: Does the chapter promise binary layout stability across major versions, and where does it tell readers how a layout change will be recorded?

critic.reasoning: The visible chapter introduction has no cross-version caveat, and readers arriving from datatype.sgml never see the one kept in protocol.sgml. The chapter hunk is truncated, so a later note cannot be excluded; one sentence would fix it.

refuted.title: Removing testlibpq3 drops the only PQexecParams binary example
refuted.failure_scenario: A C developer follows an old link or search result to libpq Example Program 3 and lands on a missing page. They now have no worked example of PQexecParams with out-of-line parameters, paramFormats and binary results. They find this out on the first visit after upgrading their docs version.
refuted.argument: The removed program's own header says its point is out-of-line parameters as well as binary I/O, so the new chapter replaces only half of it. Nobody in the thread asked for removal; in message #10 the author offered to leave testlibpq3 as it was. Removing the libpq-example-3 anchor also breaks external links to a long-published page. The commit message gives no reason beyond the example being superseded.
refuted.author_must_show: Why remove testlibpq3 and its doc example instead of keeping it as the PQexecParams example and linking it to the new chapter?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, which states the same concern more accurately. Example Program 3 is an anchor in the libpq examples section, so readers lose a link target and an example, but no page goes missing.

refuted.title: Nothing keeps the new chapter in sync with send and receive functions
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch changes a type's send function or adds a built-in type, and no one edits binary-format.sgml. A driver author codes against the chapter and sends malformed values. The mismatch shows up only as receive errors or wrong values in the field.
refuted.argument: The chapter has about 970 lines covering every built-in type, and no build or test step compares it with the send and receive functions, so a missed update fails silently. The chapter itself says the source wins on disagreement, so a stale chapter misleads exactly the readers it targets. Message #20 calls full coverage substantially more work but does not discuss upkeep. This adds one more place that type patches must remember.
refuted.author_must_show: What will remind a committer to update this chapter when a type's binary format changes or a new built-in type is added, such as a note beside each send function?

critic.reasoning: No reference documentation in Postgres is checked against the code, including the text formats in datatype.sgml, so the chapter follows existing practice. A send function change already breaks drivers today, and messages #9 and #20 asked for this documentation.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: The new chapter documents the binary wire format of every built-in type, and the patch edits protocol.sgml to link to it.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: see objection maintenance-fit-2: Removing testlibpq3 drops the only built example of binary parameters

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A chapter of about 970 lines must follow every later change to a send or receive function and every new built-in type.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why does the patch remove testlibpq3, and which libpq example then shows PQexecParams with out-of-line and binary parameters?
Does the chapter promise that binary layouts are stable across major versions, and where does it tell readers how a layout change is recorded?
Does the chapter cover every built-in type, including composite, range and multirange types, and how was each layout checked against its send function?
Why does the chapter sit under Client Interfaces when Peter Eisentraut preferred the Data Types chapter?

committability.owner_note: The owner would be a committer who knows the type send and receive functions and the frontend/backend protocol. Tom Lane took part earlier in the thread, but no committer has replied to the July 2026 patch.
committability.liability: The committer signs for the accuracy of about 970 lines of layout prose, where each error can become a driver bug. The chapter then needs an update whenever a binary format changes or a built-in type is added.
committability.author_follow_up: The author came back with a full rewrite after the 2023 Returned with Feedback and moved the entry to the next CommitFest in October 2026.

priority.reason: Direct readers are driver authors, a small group whose work reaches most users. The patch is docs-only, but a reviewer has to compare each type's prose with its send function, and both remaining objections have small fixes.

provisional_note: The chapter hunk is truncated after the first numeric types, so this review could not confirm coverage of all built-in types or the accuracy of any layout. It also could not confirm whether a later section carries a cross-version note.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add uri percent-encoding for binary data
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds 'uri' as a format for encode() and decode(), using RFC 3986 percent-encoding on binary data. The author wanted fast URL building in PL/pgSQL, for example with encode(convert_to(..., 'UTF8'), 'uri').
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson argued that the encoding ignores the URI scheme and context, so it percent-encodes delimiters such as those in https:// and the @ in userinfo, and double-encodes IPv6 zone identifiers. He suggested renaming it to 'percent-encoding' instead. The author did not send a new version addressing this feedback, and the patch no longer applied, so the entry was closed at the end of July 2020.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that uri decoding/encoding would be useful, but I'm not convinced that
this patch does the functionality justice enough to be useful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Binary I/O for isn extension
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds binary send/receive functions for the data types of the isn extension, so binary-first clients such as Npgsql can use them. The second version bumps the extension version and adds an upgrade script that sets the new functions by updating pg_type directly, because alter type cannot add send/receive functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after contrib functions were marked parallel, and the author did not send a rebased version for over a month. Robert Haas marked it Returned with Feedback at the end of the commitfest. The author said he had no time for it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So, it's been over a month since this request, and there doesn't seem
to be an update to this patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: _bt_binsrch* improvements - equal-prefix-skip binary search
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes _bt_compare and the _bt_binsrch* functions to track which key columns are already known equal from the page's high and low keys, so later comparisons skip that equal prefix during descent. It also moves the core of _bt_compare into a static inline function to cut call overhead in the binary search loops.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan noted that his earlier patch for the same idea, dynamic prefix truncation, hit a problem with concurrent page deletions. A scan that carries a skipped prefix down the tree can land on a page that no longer shares that prefix. The author agreed this makes the approach near impossible without resetting the prefix on every page, and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Concurrent page deletions could occur, which could
cause a scan that skips a prefix to miss that the page it landed on
doesn't have the same common prefix anymore.

precedents_retrieved.title: guc-ify the formerly hard-coded MAX_SEND_SIZE to max_wal_send
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch turns the hard-coded MAX_SEND_SIZE of 128 KiB, the most data walsender sends at once, into a GUC max_wal_send with an upper bound of XLOG_SEG_SIZE (16 MiB by default). The author reported about 2x better replication throughput in a lab test over high bandwidth-delay links.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author could not reproduce the earlier throughput gain in new tests, and a test machine failed. Reviewers had asked why the OS network stack would not already handle this. The patch also lacked documentation in config.sgml and had a wrong lower bound, so David Steele returned it to give the author time to test and refine it.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql export import bytea data
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql commands to load query parameters from text or binary files (\gloadfrom, earlier \set_from_file) and to save query results to files in binary form (\gbstore, later a binary \pset format). Its goal is to import and export bytea, xml and text values through psql.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on the API. Andres Freund objected that loading needs a magic $1 and allows only one column, and he asked for a general way to set query parameters. Stephen Frost disagreed with him on whether output should go to one file or to one file per cell. The last message asked for a rebase, and the visible thread shows no new version.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't like the API here much.  Loading requires knowledge of some
magic $1 value and allows only a single column, printing doesn't mean
much when there's multiple columns / rows.

precedents_retrieved.title: Escaping from blocked send() by pg_terminate_backend().
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pg_terminate_backend() end a backend blocked in send() to a client that has stopped reading. If ProcDiePending is set and select() shows the socket is still not writable after 1 second, the backend breaks the connection, for both SSL and non-SSL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show an explicit rejection. Robert Haas questioned whether send() and SSL_write() return EINTR on all platforms, and whether cutting the connection with almost no delay is too aggressive. In December 2014 Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback because the patches had not been updated after reviews. The later messages discuss a latch-based approach to waiting on the client socket, and Andres Freund pushed one part of it.
matched_queries: network byte order binary send functions
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Those patches have not been updated in a while, and I am seeing some feedback from several people, hence returning as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Send numeric version to clients (server_version_num GUC_REPORT)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Mark server_version_num as GUC_REPORT so the server sends the numeric version to network clients at connection start, next to server_version. Clients could then use it when present and fall back to parsing server_version on older servers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that clients would skip the fallback code and so fail on pre-v10 servers, and that libpq's PQserverVersion already solves this for C clients. Robert Haas agreed: clients could not rely on the new parameter for years, and by then the simpler two-part version format would make server_version easy to parse, for example with atoi(). The author accepted this and dropped the patch.
matched_queries: network byte order binary send functions
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that this would merely create an attractive nuisance: people would be very likely to omit the "fallback" code and thereby build clients that fail for no very good reason on pre-v10 servers.

precedents_retrieved.title: Replica sends an incorrect epoch in its hot standby feedback to the Master
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a bug in Postgres 9.6, 10 and 11 where a replica's nextXid can move backward during WAL replay in RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds, so hot standby feedback carries a wrong epoch and the master ignores the replica's xmin. The one-line fix advances nextXid only when the new value is higher, as similar code elsewhere does.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The withdrawal was not a rejection of the fix. The author registered the patch in the commitfest more than once, and David Steele marked the duplicate entries 2462 and 2463 as withdrawn. The visible messages show no objection, and Thomas Munro agreed the nextXid assignment looked wrong.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found, and the earlier returns in this thread (messages #17, #22, #24) were for inactivity. The patch follows the direction agreed in messages #9, #15, #19 and #20: prose only, all built-in types, a new chapter under Client Interfaces. Removing testlibpq3 goes against message #10, where the plan was to leave it unchanged, but that belongs to another angle.
No SQL syntax, GUC, catalog or pg_dump change is involved; the patch is documentation plus removal of one example program.

The patch only adds documentation and removes an example program, so it changes no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, protocol message or ABI. protocol.sgml keeps the warning that binary formats may change across server versions, so the new chapter does not freeze the wire format. Keeping the chapter in sync with send and receive functions is a maintenance question for another angle.

The patch only changes documentation and removes a test program, so it adds no privilege or exposure. Binary send and receive formats are already public in the source, and no server behaviour, default, role or access path changes. The removed testlibpq3 example sets a secure search_path, but losing that example teaches less and creates no attack path.
The patch changes only documentation, so the core idea has no hot-path, ABI or extension-fit cost. Tom Lane and Robert Haas asked for this chapter.

The only existing way is reading each type's send and receive functions in the server source, and Tom Lane (message #5, #9) and Robert Haas (message #8, #20) asked for prose docs to replace exactly that. I know of no contrib module or external tool that documents these formats, so this angle finds nothing in core or outside it that already meets the need.

The thread shows real demand. In message #4 Chapman Flack points out that every binary-protocol driver needs these layouts, and in messages #5, #9 and #20 Tom Lane and Robert Haas say real documentation would be better than reading the source. The cost is a docs-only chapter, and the removal of testlibpq3 and keeping the chapter in sync belong to other angles.
